correctness.rationale: A covering walk cannot revisit a strong component, so all intercomponent arcs must form a single directed path of components with exactly one actual arc per step. Conversely one can cover the edges within each strong component between its entry and exit. On at most three vertices a single strong component has imbalances of magnitude at most one; if there are multiple components, each is internally balanced and only the end components contribute uncancelled transition imbalances. In particular any intermediate component must be a singleton. The resulting Euler trail attains |E|+1. The independent weak-connectivity/imbalance census over all 512 masks and exact-length walk-state calculation agree with the polynomial and the 13 acyclic supports. The all-length result follows symbolically: repeat an available loop, extend the trail arbitrarily at a strongly connected terminal vertex, or pad at the cyclic end of the only remaining case, a reciprocal pair attached to a singleton by a single arc. Complete support forces the sharp threshold of ten. In the four-letter example imbalance (+2,-2,0,0) rules out length seven and the displayed eight-letter word realizes exactly the six arcs.
residual_risks: The bounded state calculation is corroboration only for the all-length statement; the padding argument is required. The theorem is for linear words and labelled alphabets.

The small-alphabet structural theorem, first failure at four, and stabilization of all exact lengths require reasoning not supplied by the general algorithm.

evidence: General feasible digram supports are walks with possibly repeated arcs. The quaternary unordered comparison has an undirected Euler-parity obstruction; the linear multiplicity record uses the Euler criterion on its prescribed counts.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The general walk formulation permits repetitions, and the unordered parity obstruction concerns a different invariant. Neither states the impossibility of forced repetitions on three vertices, nor the threshold at which all cyclic supports are realized at every length.

evidence: Bernardini et al. §1 identify equality of length-k substring sets with edge-cover walks. Karhumäki–Saarela–Zamboni define k-abelian equivalence via counts of all factors through length k.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Length-two substring-support equality is exactly the present observation; 2-abelian equivalence refines it by counts, so counts of 2-abelian classes do not enumerate its quotient.

evidence: 8ada8bf40720 refines cyclic multiplicity matrices by the number of positive off-diagonal entries. 87bc1f36ef2d counts linear ternary nine-entry multiplicity matrices at fixed length. 4aee40122a4b and 0e302c97be0b use unordered multiplicities under different hypotheses.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: These counts retain repeated edges or forget their direction and may impose circular closure or exclude runs. In particular a table of multiplicity matrices cannot be read as a table of distinct masks by merely forgetting multiplicities in its numerical totals.

originality.rationale: The distinct contribution is the exact presence-only ternary classification, sharp lossless alphabet boundary and length stabilization. Edge-cover walks in de Bruijn graphs and the general shortest-string optimization problem are already known. The closest records have different observations: cyclic or linear multiplicity matrices, sometimes with endpoints forgotten or a run restriction.
residual_risks: The 2-abelian homopolymer-free record was accessible only by indexed summary. Unindexed enumerations or earlier small-alphabet observations are possible; searches do not establish priority.

checked_sources: Bernardini et al., general shortest equivalent string problem
value.rationale: Presence-only adjacent factors are a natural information loss relative to multiplicity profiles and define an exact shortest-representative problem. The result identifies where repetitions can first be forced, classifies all ternary observations and all attainable lengths, and provides a sharp finite threshold. The structural boundary and complete attainable-length invariant make the small-alphabet census useful beyond a standalone count.
residual_risks: No support census for four or more letters, circular words, or longer factors is asserted.
